title: Klein Re-Sort — Topological Alphabet Fills the Taxonomy Gaps

banana.note: Pre-animal. No nervous system. The number 0 = null.

flatworm.note: Simplest bilateral. VENTRAL nerve cord = U shape.

jellyfish.note: Radial symmetry. Ring nerve = O shape. Dominant (43%).

centipede.note: Segmented. One pair per segment. The line = axis.

millipede.note: Two pairs per segment. Double line = doubled axis.

spider.note: 8 legs. Metastable. frac(8π) ≈ frac(π). The Klein cross-section. MISSING.

vertebrate.note: Spinal column. Full CNS/PNS. D = dorsal. Only 483 files (1%).

sponge.note: Porifera. The anti-stage. Alive but no nerves at all. The null glyph ∅.
sponge.gap: Files with no structure but that ARE alive (configs, READMEs, licenses). Fell through because they have no information entropy signal.
sponge.h_g_d_o_u_n: Pre-alphabet. Before H. The blank page.

archaea.note: Third domain of life. Extremophiles. Unique lipid membranes (ether-linked, not ester-linked). G = the spiral gate.
archaea.gap: Files that don't fit any normal classification. WGSL shaders, exotic configs, membrane protocols. They survive extreme environments (compile targets, GPU constraints).
archaea.h_g_d_o_u_n: G — the spiral fold. Archaea fold their lipids DIFFERENTLY. The G-shape IS the archaeal membrane.

octopus.nerve: DISTRIBUTED brain (each arm has own neural cluster, 2/3 of neurons in arms)
octopus.note: 8 arms like spider but INVERTED: spider centralizes (web), octopus distributes (arms). N = diagonal nerve crossing.
octopus.gap: Files that are SMART at the edges — crate lib.rs files, workspace Cargo.toml, peripheral modules. Intelligence distributed to the limbs.
octopus.h_g_d_o_u_n: N — the diagonal crossing. Each arm is an N-shaped nerve bundle.

coral.nerve: colonial nerve net (each polyp connects to neighbors)
coral.note: Colonial organism. Each polyp is an individual but together they're a reef. H = the bridge between polyps.
coral.gap: Files that are individually small but COLLECTIVELY form a structure: test files, CI configs, small helper modules. The bridge between larger organisms.
coral.h_g_d_o_u_n: H — the bridge. Coral IS an H: two columns (polyps) connected by skeleton (bridge).

fungus.nerve: mycelium network (no nerves, chemical signaling through hyphae)
fungus.note: Not animal, not plant. The mycelium network IS a nervous system without neurons. ~ = the wave, the oscillation along the network.
fungus.gap: Build artifacts, generated files, CI output, cached deps. The mycelium that connects roots (source) to fruits (binaries). The wave of compilation.
fungus.h_g_d_o_u_n: ~ — the wave operator. Mycelium oscillates nutrients like ~ oscillates between ( and ).

virus.nerve: NONE (uses host machinery, not self-replicating without host)
virus.note: Not alive by itself. Injects code into host, hijacks machinery. < = inject into host. > = extract copies. The fold operators WITHOUT a body.
virus.gap: Vendored dependencies, forked code, imported libraries. Code that came FROM somewhere else and was injected into our codebase. Alive only in context.
virus.h_g_d_o_u_n: < > — the fold operators themselves. A virus IS a fold with no body. Pure operator. Pure < >.

the_fold_cracks: sponge: alive but no structure (∅) — configs, READMEs, licenses
archaea: extreme survivors (G) — WGSL shaders, GPU kernels, membrane protocols
octopus: distributed intelligence (N) — smart peripherals, workspace Cargo.toml
coral: colonial bridges (H) — test files, CI configs, small helpers
fungus: mycelium network (~) — build artifacts, generated files, cache
virus: injected code (<>) — vendored deps, forks, imported libraries
insight: The existing taxonomy had 7 stages but used only NUMERALS and 2 letters (U, D). The Klein body adds 6 MORE stages using the full topological alphabet. What fell through was: the structureless (sponge), the extreme (archaea), the distributed (octopus), the colonial (coral), the networked (fungus), and the parasitic (virus). The fold swallowed them because they don't have a traditional AXIS — they're pre-axial, post-axial, or multi-axial. The topological alphabet catches them because it classifies by SHAPE, not hierarchy.
